question: Should ClawHub sign the existing stored hosted-feed contract, and what key id, public trust root, schema version, and rollout path should OpenClaw clients trust?
rationale: Feed signing changes a client trust boundary and production secret contract, while the current ClawHub spec explicitly leaves signed envelopes as a separate key-management decision.

options.title: Sign Stored Publications
options.body: Require the signer to wrap the current `catalogFeedPublications` payload, preserve exact version/integrity semantics, and document public-key rollout before merge.

options.title: Approve A Versioned Signed Feed
options.body: Approve a new signed schema/version only after matching OpenClaw parser support and compatibility behavior are documented.

options.title: Pause Signing
options.body: Leave this draft paused until the feed-signing RFC, production secrets, and client trust root are ready to land together.

recommendation.title: Sign Stored Publications
recommendation.body: Require the signer to wrap the current `catalogFeedPublications` payload, preserve exact version/integrity semantics, and document public-key rollout before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current hosted-feed contract and explicitly split signing into a separate production decision.
